instruction: Enable the PDF Chrome Refresh 2023 experiment in Chrome flags.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to chrome://flags and searched for 'refresh', 'ChromeRefresh2023', and 'modern'. Found some refresh-related flags when searching 'refresh' but did not find or enable the target flags. Gave up after 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate to chrome://flags, use the search box to filter flags, type URLs in address bar, interact with Chrome UI elements
metadata.failure_analysis: The target flags chrome-refresh-2023 and chrome-webui-refresh-2023 do not exist in Chrome 130. The model searched with correct intent but wrong flag names. It found related flags (ntp-realbox-cr23-theming, pdf-cr23) but did not attempt to change any dropdown values.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to enabling a single flag (pdf-cr23) that was actually visible in the trajectory when model searched 'refresh'. The flag name contains 'Chrome Refresh 2023' making it discoverable with the same search strategy the model already attempted.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to chrome://flags, finding the PDF Chrome Refresh 2023 flag, and enabling it. Evaluator restarts Chrome and checks enabled experiments include pdf-cr23. [Fixed: replaced strict list equality metric with containment check metric to handle pre-existing enabled experiments]
fix_history: Fix 1: Replaced official check_enabled_experiments (strict list equality) with custom check_enabled_experiments_contains__1656c6075ec2ba63a026b59d9c69a38f (subset/containment check) so that pre-existing enabled experiments do not cause false negatives

llm_judge_reasons: Custom metric check_enabled_experiments_contains correctly uses containment check: 'all(name in enabled_experiments_names for name in rule["names"])'. This properly verifies that pdf-cr23 is present in the enabled experiments list without requiring it to be the only enabled experiment.
Getter (enabled_experiments) correctly reads Chrome Local State file and extracts browser.enabled_labs_experiments list — the right data source for verifying enabled flags.
Postconfig correctly kills Chrome and restarts it with a 3-second sleep, ensuring the Local State file is flushed to disk before the getter reads it.
Expected value 'pdf-cr23' is the correct internal flag name for 'PDF Chrome Refresh 2023' as confirmed by trajectory observations where the flag was visible.

Parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', get_rule returns the rules dict {'type': 'names', 'names': ['pdf-cr23']} directly as the 'rule' parameter. The metric accesses rule['type'] and rule['names'] correctly.
Coverage is complete: single instruction requirement (enable one flag) with a single verification check.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: the metric splits experiment names on '@' to strip suffixes — this is correct behavior for Chrome's experiment format, but worth noting as a design choice.
